data.title: Hub Group Amends Credit Agreement to Extend Reporting Deadlines and Add EBITDA Add-Back
data.description:
Hub Group entered into a Third Amendment to its Credit Agreement to provide temporary covenant flexibility amid delayed filings and restatement work. The amendment extends the deadlines to deliver certain 2025 audited and 2026 unaudited financial statements to November 30, 2026. It also modifies the EBITDA definition to add back specified restatement-related expenses incurred on or before December 31, 2026. Management expects the changes to support liquidity and compliance while it completes its financial restatement.

  • Agreement type: Third Amendment to Credit Agreement
  • Counterparty: Bank of Montreal, as administrative agent, and the lenders

data.title: Caliber Launches Note Exchange, Refinances $3.4M; Option to Retire $9.1M at 80%
data.description:

As of September 14, 2026, the company has refinanced approximately $3.4 million and secured agreements covering an additional $9.1 million of notes eligible for discounted payoff over the next six months. data.title: October refiner sales emerge; premiums and timespreads inch up
data.description:
Asia's diesel market activity turned brisk on increased October refiner sales, with discussion levels at higher premiums amid front-month timespreads firming further.

October sales trickled in more, with at least three more refiners looking to sell off their cargoes, while discussion levels gained to single-digit premium levels.

Despite lingering uncertainty on China's October fuel exports, some refiners were selling end-September to early October cargoes.

The east-west price spread, meanwhile, hovered at discounts of more than $130 per metric ton.

Refining margins (GO10SGCKMc1) eased for a second session, falling to $81 a barrel, though such levels were still higher than the August average.

Cash differentials (GO10-SIN-DIF) inched up further to $5.76 a barrel, tracking a firmer paper market structure, though spot window activity turned lacklustre.

On the jet fuel front, spot activity ticked up as well, with both buyers and sellers in the market for October cargoes.

Taiwan's CPC Corp sought for October deliveries, in line with earlier expectations.

Some sales were done earlier in the week at premiums of $1-1.50 a barrel already for early October cargoes, trade sources said.

Regrade (JETREG10SGMc1) went into deeper discounts of nearly $4 a barrel.

SINGAPORE CASH DEALS

- No deal for jet fuel or gasoil

NEWS

- China's official data showed oil throughput rose for a second straight month in August, supported by strong fuel exports after Beijing eased export restrictions in mid-July, analysts said.

- Shipping traffic at the Strait of Hormuz dwindled further at the start of this week after attacks intensified in the Middle East, shipping data showed.

- U.S. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said on Monday a ban on U.S. oil or fuel exports would be unlikely to help lower energy prices for consumers amidst the Iran war.

- Half of Russia's six top diesel-producing refineries were forced to significantly cut back or completely halt output in September due to damage sustained in drone attacks, according to Reuters calculations based on data from fuel market participants.

data.title: Lifecare ASA: Share capital increase registered
data.description:
Reference is made to the stock exchange announcement by Lifecare ASA (the "Company") on 11 September 2026 regarding the completion of the acquisition of Ocean TuniCell AS.

The share capital increase pertaining to the issuance of the consideration shares has now been registered with the Norwegian Register of Business Enterprises. The Company's new share capital is NOK 43,036,196.00 divided into 430,361,960 shares, each with a nominal value of NOK 0.10.

The new shares will be delivered to the VPS accounts of the subscribers to whom they are allocated on or about 15 September 2026. The new shares may not be traded by subscribers until they are received on the respective subscriber's VPS account.

20,914,068 of the consideration shares are subject to lock-up obligations for a period of nine months from completion of the transaction on the terms and conditions of the share purchase agreement.

About us

Lifecare ASA is a medical sensor company developing technology for sensing and monitoring of various body analytes. Lifecare's focus is to bring the next generation of Continuous Glucose Monitoring systems to market. Lifecare enables osmotic pressure as sensing principle. Lifecare's sensor technology is suitable for identifying and monitoring the occurrence of a wide range of analytes and molecules in the human body and in pets.

data.title: Rupee drops with stocks, bonds as oil, inflation and Fed worries mount
data.description:
By Jaspreet Kalra

The Indian rupee fell to its weakest level in more than a month on Tuesday but held above 96 per dollar as likely central bank intervention limited losses driven by surging oil prices and bets on a U.S. rate hike this week.

The rupee settled at 95.9550 per dollar, down xx% on the day, its biggest one-day fall since mid-July.

Brent crude rose more than 2% to $108.20 a barrel, raising concerns about a wider Indian trade deficit and higher inflation.

Data on Tuesday showed that India's goods trade deficit was narrower than anticipated in August, largely on account of a drop in gold imports, at $26.8 billion against economist expectations of about $32 billion.

Meanwhile, signs of broadening inflation have prompted traders to add to wagers on a rate hike by the Reserve Bank of India next month.

Both Citi and Deutsche Bank brought forward rate hikes calls from December to October.

This also weighed on government bonds with the benchmark 10-year bond yield climbing to its highest since mid-May.

Stocks were under pressure as well with the benchmark Nifty 50 index ending lower by about 1%.

"A gradual broadening of price pressures is likely to keep inflation readings above 5% in second half of the fiscal year, underscoring the need for a tighter (monetary) policy bias," Radhika Rao, senior economist at DBS said in a note.

She expects the goods trade deficit to remain around $30 billion as stronger exports are offset by a further widening in the energy import bill.

In addition to oil prices, focus is also on the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy decision on Wednesday with markets pricing a 93% chance of a hike. The Bank of Japan is also expected to raise rates on Friday.

data.title: Sinch AB: Shoppers are cautious about AI, but confident when it has a job to do
data.description:
STOCKHOLM, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- New research from Sinch AB (publ), shows a nuanced picture of shoppers' attitudes to AI ahead of Black Friday and the holiday season: broader concerns remain, while confidence is high when AI is used for specific, practical tasks. Among 2,501 consumers across eight markets, only 43% think AI will make their holiday shopping easier this year, down from 48% in 2025. Privacy remains shoppers' top reservation about AI for the second year running, cited by 43%, and just 7% say they have no concerns about it at all.

That caution does not carry over once the task is specific. 81% of shoppers say they are confident an AI assistant can handle order tracking and shipping updates, while 74% say the same for pre-purchase questions.  Confidence is lower, but still substantial, for account changes (66%) and payment or billing changes (62%).

Shoppers are also open to interacting with AI. Of the 2,501 people surveyed, only one said they would never want to interact with an AI chatbot under any circumstance. The most popular use cases were order tracking (48%), researching a product before buying (47%), and getting customer service (36%).

"AI for AI's sake doesn't land with shoppers, but AI attached to a job they actually want done does. Order tracking and pre-purchase questions are the easy wins, where confidence is already high. Payment, billing and account changes are different: shoppers still want a human close by, and brands need to make that handoff easy and obvious," said Robert Gerstmann, Chief Evangelist and Co-Founder of Sinch.

Trust follows a similar split when AI gives advice rather than just information. 53% of shoppers trust a real person's product recommendation over AI's, while 47% trust AI just as much or more. For voice interactions, 48% trust a human phone agent over an AI voice agent, while 37% trust the AI equally or more.

Confidence in AI also varies sharply by market. The US is the most AI-skeptical market surveyed: just 26% of shoppers think AI will make their holiday shopping easier, and 43% say it won't. Brazil is at the opposite end, with 78% of the surveyed shoppers saying AI will make their shopping easier this year.

Other key findings:

  • 43% think AI will make their holiday shopping easier this year, down from 48% in 2025
  • Privacy or data use is shoppers' top AI concern, cited by 43%; only 7% say they have no concerns at all
  • 81% are confident an AI assistant can handle order tracking and shipping updates; confidence falls to 62% for payment or billing changes
  • Only 1 of 2,501 respondents said they would never want to interact with an AI chatbot
  • 53% trust a real person's product recommendation over AI's; 47% trust AI just as much or more
  • 48% trust a human phone agent more than an AI voice agent, while 37% trust both equally and 15% want the option to transfer to a human if needed.
  • The US is the most AI-skeptical market surveyed (26% of the surveyed shoppers think AI will help, 43% say it won't); Brazil is the most optimistic (78% of the surveyed shoppers)

About the research

The findings are based on an online survey of 2,501 consumers in the United States (698), Australia (351), Brazil (350), the United Kingdom (252), France (225), Germany (225), Mexico (200) and Spain (200), conducted by Sinch in 2026.

The 2026 study follows Sinch's previous BFCM consumer research. India and Canada were included in the 2025 sample but not in 2026. Full country-level data is available on request. Read more about the survey here.

data.title: ZAWYA: AmCham Oman and Ministry of Health advance US FDA, export readiness for Oman’s medical manufacturers
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Muscat – AmCham Oman, in partnership with the Ministry of Health’s Department of Investment Empowerment and Invest Oman, hosted the USFDA and Export Readiness Seminar: Unlocking Oman’s Medical Manufacturing Potential on 14 September at Invest Oman.

The seminar brought together approximately 40 representatives from Oman’s pharmaceutical, medical device, healthcare distribution and supporting sectors, alongside government officials and representatives of the banking sector. Sohar International and Credit Oman supported the programme as official Event Partners. Designed to strengthen the export capabilities of manufacturers based in Oman, the seminar provided practical guidance for companies seeking to enter the U.S. healthcare market. Sessions addressed U.S. Food and Drug Administration requirements, regulatory approvals, export readiness, investment opportunities, trade finance and export credit insurance.

H.E. Dr Ahmed bin Salem Al Mandhari, Undersecretary for Health Planning and Regulation at the Ministry of Health, opened the seminar and thanked AmCham Oman for its collaboration and the Department of Investment Empowerment for supporting investors in Oman and helping them explore opportunities beyond the Sultanate.

H.E. Dr Al Mandhari acknowledged the investment and effort made by manufacturers to develop Oman’s medical and pharmaceutical industries, as well as their continued work to meet quality and compliance standards.

He noted that an industrial survey conducted by the Department of Investment Empowerment showed that the sector had entered a new phase of growth. This growth is supported by increasing investor confidence, a rising number of factories and projects, and expanding opportunities for investment. He also reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to increasing the localisation of pharmaceutical manufacturing in Oman, emphasising that continued progress would require collaboration, sustained commitment and further development of the achievements already made.

“Oman’s medical and pharmaceutical manufacturing sector is entering a promising new phase, supported by growing investor confidence, new factories and expanding opportunities. By working together to strengthen quality, compliance and export readiness, we can support local manufacturers, increase pharmaceutical localisation and open new pathways into international markets,” H.E. Dr Al Mandhari said.

Rebecca Olson, CEO of AmCham Oman, highlighted the commercial opportunities available to Omani manufacturers in the United States and AmCham Oman’s role in helping companies navigate the export journey. “Oman has capable manufacturers, strong products and a growing healthcare ecosystem. The opportunity now is to help companies understand precisely what is required to compete internationally and connect them with the right regulatory, commercial and financial expertise,” Olson said.

“Our role at AmCham Oman is to serve as a bridge, supporting Omani manufacturers with the knowledge, regulatory guidance and export readiness pathways they need to approach the U.S. market with confidence.”

Harshal Dutia, Director of Trade and Investment at AmCham Oman, guided participants through the requirements and practical considerations involved in preparing products manufactured in Oman for export to the United States. His session also examined the U.S.-Oman Free Trade Agreement, which has been in force since 2009, and the customs advantages it offers for eligible Omani goods entering the United States. “Export readiness requires more than identifying a promising market. Manufacturers must

understand product classification, documentation, labelling, quality systems, regulatory responsibilities and the commercial realities of entering that market. This seminar helped companies assess where they currently stand and identify the practical steps they need to take next,” Dutia said.

The programme also featured Lisa Svinina, Head of the Pharma Business Unit at MROVIN, who addressed regulatory clearance and approval processes. Rabee Al Qadhi, Head of Global Trade Solutions at Sohar International, outlined trade finance solutions available to manufacturers pursuing international growth. Mohammed Al Jabri, Senior Sales Manager at Credit Oman SAOC, discussed export credit insurance and strategies for managing commercial risk when entering new markets.

By the conclusion of the seminar, participating companies had gained a clearer understanding of U.S. FDA requirements and the practical steps involved in preparing to enter the U.S. market. The programme also connected manufacturers with specialists in regulation, investment, international trade, finance and export risk management. The seminar highlighted several opportunities for continued support, including follow-up meetings with participating manufacturers, export readiness assessments, regulatory

consultations, targeted workshops and connections with U.S.-based specialists. These opportunities can be developed according to the products, needs and readiness of participating companies.

The initiative forms part of wider efforts to help Omani medical and pharmaceutical manufacturers understand the requirements of international markets, strengthen direct engagement with relevant government and financial institutions, and explore potential

partnerships and future areas of cooperation. It also supports the objectives of Oman Vision 2040 by contributing to economic diversification, pharmaceutical localisation and the development of national healthcare system.
